text:
incident-bot: ALERT: kv-cache continuous-batching error rate spike detected in us-west-2 / p99 latency > 5s across inference pool. Auto-escalation: paging on-call.

alice: acked — oncall here. seeing huge cache growth and latency. linking to dashboards: https://redwood/dashboards/kv-cache/3559876543

bob: observed sudden number of partial-evictions + allocator churn. RX logs show repeated arena allocations then immediate frees.

claire: perf traces indicate continuous batching backlog spikes. many requests getting large batch sizes > 128 unexpectedly.

dan: reproducing locally — continuous_batching seems to backpressure poorly when kv-cache grows, causing batch fanout. suspect KV cache fragmentation causing malloc spikes in pytorch cuda.

emily: customer impact — a few enterprise customers reporting timeouts in production (chat widgets). CS notified.

alice: immediate mitigation options? can we dial back batching window or force small max batch size per request type?

bob: propose: 1) reduce continuous_batching.burst_window_ms from 2000 -> 200; 2) set continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens=4096 -> 1024 for canary; 3) force kv_allocator.arena_release_pct=0.25 to release memory more aggressively.

claire: also disable prefix/KV caching for canary model variant — prefix caching + fragmentation seems to correlate with the leak. disabling reduces KV cache working set.

dan: I can push a config hotfix to the runtime and canary-deploy. PR: https://git.redwood/inference/runtime/pulls/4512

deploy-bot: build started for commit 7a9f3d2 -> CI: 8/9 passed

alice: who owns customer comms if we need to send a status note?

emily: I'll draft a short message: "We are investigating latency for model endpoints in us-west-2, mitigations in progress — minimal impact to most customers."

frank: keep it vague and avoid root cause until confirmed. good.

bob: logs snippet from affected node (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-15T02:14:27Z] kv_cache.cpp:evict() evicted=64 free_slots=32 total_slots=8192
[2026-03-15T02:14:28Z] allocator.cu:arena_alloc() size=134217728 arena=3 MALLOC succeeded
[2026-03-15T02:14:28Z] allocator.cu:arena_release() released=0 threshold=0.5
[2026-03-15T02:14:29Z] runtime:batch_scheduler.cpp batch_size=192 queued=94 p99=6.2s
```

claire: that's classic: arena_release not releasing because fragmentation below threshold -> repeated large allocations -> cuda OOM risk if sustained.

alice: (decision) execute hotfix: disable prefix cache for model:open-*-r1, set burst_window_ms=200, max_batch_tokens=1024, arena_release_pct=0.25. Apply to 10% canary in us-west-2 immediately.

dan: applying now. Rolling config to canary 10% -> will monitor for 5 minutes then increase. Deploy link: https://deploy.redwood/rollouts/3559876543

deploy-bot: canary rollout started -> 10% instances in us-west-2.

bob: added a temporary metric alert: kv_cache_evictions_per_min > 50 -> pager.

alice: monitoring Dash: p99 latency dropping?

claire: 60s in: p99 down from 6.2s -> 2.1s on canary nodes. KV working set reduced ~38%.

frank: good signal. any side effects? quality regressions from disabling prefix cache?

claire: quick A/B on generation perf — negligible quality delta, ~0.3% tokengen latency increase on disabled nodes but overall end-to-end improved.

emily: sent customer status update v1 to affected customers.

alice: increase canary to 40% for 10 min.

dan: done. 40% rolling -> all in us-west healthy so far.

deploy-bot: rollout at 40% complete. no deploy failures.

bob: allocator telemetry: arena_release events increased ~4x after change, fragmentation ratio down from 0.61 -> 0.28.

alice: good. let's keep changes for 24h while we triage root cause and prepare a proper allocator hotpatch.

claire: next steps: reproduce minimal repro, add fuzz tests for continuous_batching config combos, and write a small allocator test that simulates prefix cache churn to validate arena_release heuristics. I'll own.

dan: I'll draft the runtime hotpatch to apply a low-cost compaction pass on arena free lists and adjust `cudaMallocAsync` fallback policy. PR: https://git.redwood/inference/runtime/pulls/4513

bob: ops note: create runbook entry for this class of incidents: include quick mitigations (disable prefix cache, reduce burst window, force arena_release), and instrument `arena_fragmentation_ratio` + `continuous_batching.queue_depth` thresholds. I'll author.

alice: thanks — assign follow-ups:
- claire: reproduce + tests + patch timeline (ETA 24h)
- dan: runtime hotpatch PR (ETA 48h)
- bob: runbook + alert tuning (ETA 6h)
- emily: customer comms + followup (ongoing)

emily: scheduled customer follow-up email for 30m with updates.

frank: will prepare postmortem scope once stable. include cost impact estimate.

alice: closing loop: raising incident to sev-2 (customer visible but mitigated). Pushing final status in 30m. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity set -> sev-2, runbook assigned, incident lead -> alice.

alice: thanks all. I'll leave this thread open for new observations — please call if you see regressions.

bob: note for postmortem: check for a related recent change in prefix caching logic rolled ~48h ago (commit f2b8c4a).

claire: copying logs and traces to the incident folder: https://s3.redwood/incidents/3559876543/traces.zip

deploy-bot: rollout completed to 40% stable; canary metrics passed.

alice: last check: p99 now ~1.9s cluster-wide, evictions normalized. setting last_message_ts to 3559876680 for record. thanks everyone.
